note: Screen Recording 2026-09-05 002254.mp4 at 8s, the bare rifle. The clip goes
on for another hundred seconds and most of it is unusable for artwork: at
27s Al puts a bright pink appearance on the rifle and never takes it off.
Everything cut from this weapon's own picture has to come from the first
twenty-six seconds. Text does not care about the skin, so the slot lists

The box stops at x1628 rather than running to the stock's chip, because on
this rifle the Rear Grip chip sits at x1673 -- only 45px past the end of the
buttstock. A box wide enough to be comfortable would have taken the chip
into the weapon's own silhouette.
FIFTEEN BASE SLOTS, the most of any weapon here, and all three patches are
on the bare rifle. On the MCX LT the side patches are brought by a barrel
and on the RM277 there is no upper patch at all; this one simply has the
lot. Which is the third different answer three weapons have given to the
question of whose slots the patches are.
Seeds are the chip's TOP-LEFT corner, not its centre -- the same as every
other spec here. Written as centres the first time, which put all fifteen
35px down and right of the box, and the snap then locked each one onto a
weak local maximum a few pixels away rather than the border it was meant
to find. The ring scores gave it away: 3 and 4 against the MCX LT's 17.
